item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 041726
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Sun Oct 4 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Nolo, located well to the west-northwest of the main Hawaiian
Islands, and on Hurricane Rachel, located a few hundred miles
southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

South of Southern Mexico:
A broad area of low pressure is forecast to develop over the next
day or so just to the south of the Gulf of Tehuantepec. Thereafter,
environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual development,
and a tropical depression is expected to form during the middle to
latter portion of the week while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward to northwestward, just offshore of the southern
to southwestern coast of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Sun Oct 04 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 042032
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Advisory Number  31
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 PM MST Sun Oct 04 2026
 
...RACHEL MAINTAINING ITS STRENGTH...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM MST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.1N 114.3W
ABOUT 340 MI...550 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...105 MPH...165 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...965 MB...28.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM MST (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located 
near latitude 20.1 North, longitude 114.3 West. Rachel is moving 
toward the west near 6 mph (9 km/h). A continued slow motion is 
expected through the middle of the week.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 105 mph (165 km/h) with higher
gusts. Fluctuations in strength are possible through tonight, but 
Rachel is expected to slowly weaken beginning on Monday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles
(220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 965 mb (28.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will continue to affect the coast
of the Baja California Peninsula through Monday. These swells are
likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 31
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Sun Oct 04 2026 
464 
WTPZ43 KNHC 042032
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  31
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 PM MST Sun Oct 04 2026
 
Rachel has not changed much during the past several hours. The
hurricane continues to have a well established inner core, but the
eye has become a little more cloud-filled and ragged compared to
this morning. The latest satellite intensity estimates range from
85 to 97 kt, and based on that data and the relatively steady
state appearance of the system, the initial intensity is held at 90
kt. A 1616 UTC ASCAT-B was helpful in adjusting the initial wind
radii.
 
The hurricane has turned westward over the past several hours, with
the initial motion now estimated to be 270/5 kt. A high pressure
system to the north of Rachel should keep the system on a slow
westward track through the middle of the week. After that time, the
high is expected to weaken and shift eastward as a trough cuts off
near the southern California coast, which should allow Rachel to
turn back to the west-northwest by the end of the week. Little
change was made to the previous track forecast, and this one lies
near the best-performing models of the year so far, HCCA and GDMI.
 
Rachel will likely maintain its strength through tonight. However,
as the hurricane moves farther west, it will be entering a
progressively drier airmass and moving over sub 26C waters in a
couple of days. Therefore, steady weakening is forecast to begin on
Monday and continue through the week. The NHC intensity forecast
lies generally near the middle of the guidance envelope, and is
largely an update of the previous one.
